newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Greens seek ban on plutonium air freight.
newsitem.headline: German Greens seek ban on plutonium air freight.

text.p: Green party Environment ministers in four German states have called for a ban on the transportation by air of plutonium fuel rods.
The German government should follow the example of the U.S.with tough restrictions on airborne transport of plutonium materials, they said in a joint statement.

Their demand will be discussed at a forthcoming meeting of state environment ministers, Margarethe Nimsch (Hesse), Baerbel Hoehn (North Rhine Westphalia), Heidrun Heideke (Saxony-Anhalt) and Rainer Steenblock (Schleswig-Holstein) said.
The ministers warned plutonium roads from the nuclear plant at Hanau, central Germany, could be flown from Frankfurt airport and new rods might be brought in from Britain by air.

Greenpeace warned on October 7 that contracts between British Nuclear Fuels (BNFL) and utilities in Germany and Switzerland could lead to more than 100 "nuclear flights" over the next two to five years.
The traffic covered the shipment of spent nuclear fuel to BNFL sites in Britain for reprocessing and the return of the fuel to the client.
